:::{#thm-matvec-linear}
#### A matrix maps a combination to the same combination of images

If $\matr{A}$ is an $m \times n$ matrix,
$\vecf{z}_1, \ldots, \vecf{z}_k \in \reals^n$
and $c_1, \ldots, c_k \in \reals$, then

$$
\matr{A}\,(c_1 \vecf{z}_1 + \cdots + c_k \vecf{z}_k)
= c_1\,\matr{A} \vecf{z}_1 + \cdots + c_k\,\matr{A} \vecf{z}_k.
$$

:::

::: proof

Write $z_{ij}$ for entry $j$ of $\vecf{z}_i$,
so entry $j$ of $\sum_i c_i \vecf{z}_i$ is $\sum_i c_i z_{ij}$.
Compare entry $r$ of the two sides, for each $r = 1, \ldots, m$:

$$
\ba
\paren{\matr{A} \sum_{i=1}^{k} c_i \vecf{z}_i}_r
&= \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{rj} \sum_{i=1}^{k} c_i z_{ij}
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= \sum_{j=1}^{n} \sum_{i=1}^{k} a_{rj}\,c_i z_{ij}
&& \text{(distribute } a_{rj} \text{ over the inner sum)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{k} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{rj}\,c_i z_{ij}
&& \text{(reorder the finite double sum)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{k} \sum_{j=1}^{n} c_i\,a_{rj} z_{ij}
&& \text{(multiplication of numbers is commutative)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{k} c_i \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{rj} z_{ij}
&& \text{(factor } c_i \text{ out of the inner sum)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{k} c_i\,(\matr{A} \vecf{z}_i)_r
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\ea
$$

which is entry $r$ of $\sum_i c_i\,\matr{A} \vecf{z}_i$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-matvec-linear}
#### Applying a matrix to a combination

Let $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$,
$\vecf{z}_1 = (1, 0)$ and $\vecf{z}_2 = (0, 1)$.
Then $\matr{A} \vecf{z}_1 = (1, 3)$ and $\matr{A} \vecf{z}_2 = (2, 4)$,
and for the combination $2 \vecf{z}_1 - \vecf{z}_2 = (2, -1)$:

$$
\ba
\matr{A}\,(2, -1)
&= (1 \cd 2 + 2 \cd (-1),\; 3 \cd 2 + 4 \cd (-1))
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= (0, 2)
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\\
&= 2\,(1, 3) - (2, 4),
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

which is $2\,\matr{A} \vecf{z}_1 - \matr{A} \vecf{z}_2$, as @thm-matvec-linear says.

:::
